en.title: Boeing to Cut About 2,500 Commercial Airplanes Jobs as Production Ramp-Up Slows
en.summary: Boeing will cut about 5% of its Commercial Airplanes workforce, around 2,500 jobs, through involuntary layoffs and natural attrition, with layoff notifications starting in December; the move follows slower production increases for the 737 MAX and 787 amid factory and supply-chain challenges.
body: Boeing has announced it will reduce its Boeing Commercial Airplanes (BCA) workforce by around 5%, affecting about 2,500 workers, through involuntary layoffs and natural attrition. Layoff notifications will start in December, and no layoffs are expected in November. The decision comes as Boeing confirmed it plans to slow factory production rate increases as a result of factory and supply chain challenges.

Boeing Commercial Airplanes CEO Stephanie Pope shared a memo to employees, as reported by CNBC: "Adjusting our production schedules and reducing aircraft output puts us in an overstaffed position. Unfortunately, that means we need to align our staffing levels to our revised business plans." In a statement obtained by Simple Flying, a Boeing spokesperson confirmed that "as we adjust our production plans, we are aligning staffing levels to those updated plans and the overall needs of the business. Over the coming months, we will reduce Commercial Airplanes staffing by about five percent through a combination of attrition and layoffs." Boeing Commercial Airplanes employs a total of 50,494 workers, and Boeing said its team is working to minimize the impact on teammates through company-sponsored outplacement services, layoff benefits and employee assistance program support.

The decision stems from challenges in assembly lines and component delivery flows, requiring Boeing to recalibrate to its current supply chain abilities instead of aggressive output targets. The 737 MAX target timeline of 47 planes per month has been pushed out until mid to late 2027, with the lift from 47 to 52 jets per month pushed out until the second half of 2027; output increases on the 787 Dreamliner have also been reduced. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg told investors last month that MAX production will not increase until the second half of 2027, with 737 and 787 output remaining at 47 and eight jets per month and disruption hampering the 767 and 777 programs. Despite the changes, Boeing continues to hold a backlog of more than 6,300 airplanes, valued in excess of $610 billion.

zh.title: 波音民航部門裁員約2500人，737MAX與787增產放緩
zh.summary: 波音宣布民航部門將裁減約5%人力、約2500個職位，透過非自願裁員與自然流失進行，11月不裁員、12月起發出裁員通知；主因是工廠與供應鏈挑戰迫使737MAX與787放慢增產步伐。
body: 波音宣布將裁減民航部門約5%人力，約2500個職位，透過非自願裁員與自然流失進行。波音民航部門執行長Stephanie Pope在致員工的備忘錄中表示，調整生產時程並減少產量後人力已過剩，必須讓人力水準符合修訂後的業務計畫。裁員通知將於12月開始發出，11月不會裁員。
波音發言人向Simple Flying證實，隨著生產計畫調整，公司正讓人力水準符合更新後的計畫與整體業務需求，未來數月將透過自然流失與裁員相結合的方式，裁減民航部門約5%人力。波音民航部門共雇用50494名員工。波音表示，團隊正透過公司贊助的轉職協助、裁員福利與員工協助計畫，盡量減輕對員工的影響。

這次調整源自組裝線與零組件交付流程的挑戰，波音必須依目前供應鏈能力重新校準，而非追求積極的產量目標。737MAX月產47架的目標時程延至2027年中後期，提升至52架的時程則延至2027年下半年；787增產步伐亦放緩。波音執行長Kelly Ortberg上月向投資人表示，MAX產量在2027年下半年前不會提升；737與787產量將維持每月47架與8架，767與777計畫亦受干擾。儘管如此，波音仍握有逾6300架飛機訂單，價值逾6100億美元。
